judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition covers names, federal employer identification numbers, organizational identification numbers, state of organization and "organizational identity," but the proviso permitting change on 30 days' notice is expressed only as to "names" — so four of the five prohibited changes appear to have no escape route.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.7 and Schedules 5.7(a)-(c) record the very identifiers this covenant freezes, and Section 4.4(a) covers the financing-statement mechanics; nothing else supplies the missing permission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening carve-outs — including "the curtailment in the origination of new loans" — permit precisely the kind of change the covenant otherwise forbids, and "the principal nature of its or their business" is imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.14(b)(i) contemplates proceeds being used to make new loans while this covenant expressly blesses curtailing origination; read with the Permitted Reorganization carve-out, the covenant's remaining field of operation is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated prohibitions with defined carve-outs; the drafting is dense but each limb is specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (c) restricts amendments only to Indebtedness "permitted under Section 7.1(b)" (Schedule 5.20 debt), leaving Subordinated Debt and Approved Debt documents unrestricted here although Section 7.7(b) deals with payments on them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence keyed entirely to a defined term; nothing ambiguous in the covenant itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Change of Control" definition requires Permitted Holders (four named individuals) to own 100% of Manager and Servicer, which is difficult to reconcile with the "Permitted Reorganization" definition's contemplation of admitting new members and managers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Advance notice" is given no period, and "in any material respect" is the only threshold, so both the trigger and the procedure are indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Borrower's Required Procedures" definition already requires that any amendment have Lender's prior written approval "given or withheld in Lender's sole discretion," a stricter and differently worded control than this covenant's notice-and-consent formulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference to the quarterly financials is garbled, and clause (a)(ii) permits return-of-capital distributions "to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents" — a permission whose content lies outside the instrument and could swallow the prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Restricted Payments" clause (e) catches any payment to a Stock holder "not expressly authorized in this Agreement," so the breadth of this exception determines the covenant's whole content; Section 7.3(a) restricts amendment of the Governing Documents but does not fix them in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear prohibitions with a GAAP carve-out and a specified condition for accounting-firm arrangements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1, 6.3 and the GAAP definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and keyed to defined terms; "incur any liabilities (including contingent obligations) for or in connection with any Investment" is broad but bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Investments expressly includes making Notes Receivable and holding Real Estate Owned, so the Borrowers' core business is carved out; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is headed "Transactions with Affiliates" but its first sentence prohibits forming or acquiring any Subsidiary, an unrelated subject, and clause (c) then permits "any other transaction" satisfying four cumulative conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Subsidiary" definition excludes any entity formed after the Closing Date that is not funded with Borrower assets, plus any New Fund and Bar-K, so the no-new-Subsidiary sentence can be circumvented without breach; the Affiliate definition's 10% deeming rule applies specifically "for purposes of… Section 7.13".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two enumerated permitted uses; "working capital and general corporate needs" is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (b)(i) permits proceeds only for loans "evidenced by an Eligible Note Receivable," which is a stricter standard than the Note Receivable definition; consistent with Section 6.18's disbursement mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition with a narrow, specific proviso for loan files; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 5.5's representation and Section 4.4(d)'s assignment of storage access rights; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single objective dollar test measured monthly; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Triggering Event" definition uses a $500,000,000 Notes Receivable test and Section 3.1(n) the same $600,000,000 figure; the tension is with Section 7.16(b), whose 0.9% ratio against this floor caps borrowing far below the facility size.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled ("a Senior Leverage Ratio (expressed as a percentage) that is of no greater than") and the figure — nine-tenths of one percent — is on its face implausible for a leverage covenant, so either the words or the number must be wrong.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Against the Section 7.16(a) $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor, a 0.9% ratio caps Obligations at roughly $5.4 million, which cannot be reconciled with the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount, Section 2.1(a) or the $20,000,000 minimum-balance fee assumptions in Sections 2.10(c) and 2.10(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A percentage test measured monthly; the numeral is clear even though the words are OCR-garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on "Defaulted Note Receivable," which either Administrative Borrower or Lender may unilaterally "deem" applicable, so one party can move the covenant's numerator at will.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional payment default with an itemised description of the amounts covered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Obligations and Lender Expenses definitions and Section 2.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three-tier structure is clear, but clause (a) lists Section 6.15 among the no-cure covenants and clause (c) refers to "a condition subsequent set forth in Section 3.2" — a numbering that does not appear in the printed document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.15 is "[Intentionally Omitted]" and the conditions-subsequent section is printed as "4.2," so two of this provision's cross-references point at nothing; Section 6.4 is likewise blank and correctly omitted, which shows the list was meant to be exact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any material portion" is an undefined quantum, and the trigger "comes into the possession of any third Person" is drafted so broadly that ordinary custodial or servicing arrangements would satisfy it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 4.2, 5.5, 6.9 and 7.15 all contemplate Collateral being held by a custodian for Lender or stored in a public warehouse, so the literal words of this default trigger against arrangements the Agreement requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Insolvency Proceeding definition and the automatic acceleration paragraph at the end of Section 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Not timely controverted" is undefined, and the proviso attached to clause (ii) refers to "the pendency of such period" although clause (ii) states no period — the sentence has lost a component.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in substance with Section 9.1's automatic acceleration on a Section 8.5 default and with the Insolvency Proceeding definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All or any material part of its business affairs" is a soft quantum in an otherwise clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.3(c)'s injunction condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "whether choate or otherwise" is an unusual and imprecise legal formulation, and the trigger sweeps in any tax or debt owing to any governmental agency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens clause (b) and the Permitted Protest definition permit contested tax liens, but this default has no Permitted Protest carve-out on its face — a gap between the covenant regime and the default trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean dollar threshold with a defined consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens clause (j) permits "Liens resulting from any judgment or award that is not an Event of Default hereunder," which defines the permission by reference to this default and this default by reference to the lien — a circular pair.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The qualifier "the termination of which is reasonably likely to result in a Material Adverse Change" is placed after limb (z) only, so whether it also limits limbs (x) and (y) is genuinely open — a scope-of-modifier problem compounded by the mangled limb labels.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (x) reaches defaults on "capital obligations to any member or former member," which Section 7.10 and the Permitted Reorganization definition both contemplate being restructured, so the unqualified reading would be harsh.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear and self-limiting by reference to the applicable subordination terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.7(b) and 7.10(b) and the Subordination Agreement definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Material misstatement or misrepresentation" in any "warranty, representation, statement, or Record" is broad but the standard is familiar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.4 deems any transmitted Record a representation of accuracy and completeness, which widens this default considerably; Section 6.14 says notification of a prior misstatement does not cure it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, specific trigger; the grammar ("the obligations… is terminated") is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Validity Agreement and Validity Agreement Party definitions and Section 3.1(b)(iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Become unable to perform" is undefined, and the replacement must have qualifications "acceptable to Lender" with no reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Executive Officer" names five individuals employed by Manager or Servicer, and Servicer is expressly excluded from the Subsidiary group, so this default reaches persons outside the credit group.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in structure, with carve-outs for permitted dispositions and for priority permitted by the Loan Documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.9(e) already represents the Liens are perfected and first priority, and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (s) treats perfection as an ongoing condition — three provisions imposing overlapping perfection standards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, materiality-qualified trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on the Servicing Agreement, a document defined but not reproduced; Sections 4.8 and 9.1(e)/(o) also key off it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Materiality is fixed by whatever "Lender in its Permitted Discretion deems to be material," and the provision trails off with a dangling "or."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.4 makes each provision severable for enforceability purposes, which sits oddly with a default triggered by any material provision being declared void.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in amount with a stated three-Business-Day cure; "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender" is the soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e) and 4.2 each state the same $250,000,000 requirement in different words, so the trigger's precise content depends on which formulation governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional remedies chapeau expressly subject to the Code's commercial-reasonableness requirement, plus a plain acceleration right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.4, 3.6 and 9.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; entirely clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.3(b) and 3.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear and carefully limited to future obligations of Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.6's survival provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "For amounts and upon terms which Lender considers advisable" gives an unqualified discretion, but the netting mechanic is specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.5(f) grants the same power under a "Permitted Discretion" standard, so the two provisions state different standards for the same act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing parenthetical charges all amounts incurred as "Lender Group Expenses," a term that is defined nowhere in the Agreement — the cost-shifting mechanism therefore has no defined content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 defines "Lender Expenses," which the Section 2.3(b) waterfall pays first and Section 2.5(c) charges to the Loan Account; whether "Lender Group Expenses" means the same thing is left to inference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad self-help powers with a licence to occupy premises; "considers necessary or reasonable" is soft but the acts are enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 10's self-help and Section 4.4(d)'s storage-access assignment; the reference to "any Guarantor" is another remnant of an absent party.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed setoff right with an express waiver of advance notice and a post-hoc notice obligation; carefully drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6(d) (Cash Management Accounts as cash collateral) and Section 9.1(h).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.6(d), 3.6 and 9.1(g).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The remedies enumerated — ship, finish, repair, complete production of, advertise for sale — belong to an inventory-based facility and have little application to a portfolio of promissory notes, so their reach here is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Borrower Collateral" here consists overwhelmingly of Notes Receivable and Deposit Accounts, and Sections 9.1(e) and (o) supply the remedies actually fitted to that collateral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear and tied to the commercial-reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Section 9.1 chapeau and Section 9.1(k)'s notice mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to form and 15-day period, though the carve-out for collateral that is "perishable" or "customarily sold on a recognized market" is inapt for this collateral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs notice "as provided in Section 12," and Section 12 has a special deemed-sent rule for Code enforcement notices; the two mesh.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substance is a single sentence, but the subsection is lettered "(h)" in a run that has already used (h) — the enumeration is corrupted at this point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2 and other provisions cross-refer to lettered subsections elsewhere, so corrupted lettering within Section 9.1 is a live risk of mis-citation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear, with an express "to the maximum extent permitted by law" limit on the ex parte element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.2's cumulative-remedies provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A catch-all reserving "all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity," and the subsection is lettered "(m)" duplicating the preceding one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.2 states the same principle again with the qualifier "not inconsistent herewith," which this subsection omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It again charges amounts as "Lender Group Expenses," an undefined term, and folds an automatic-acceleration paragraph into a lettered remedy sub-clause where it does not belong.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It largely duplicates Section 9.1(e), and the automatic acceleration on Sections 8.4/8.5 sits against the Section 9.1 chapeau's premise that remedies are exercised "at [Lender's] election".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional cumulative-remedies and non-waiver clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1(n) and 15.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lender may act "in its sole discretion and without prior notice," and the closing sentence makes an official payment notice "conclusive evidence" of validity — strong but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (b) lets Lender set reserves against the Borrowing Base or the Maximum Revolver Amount "as Lender deems necessary," with none of the Permitted Discretion or Triggering Event limits that Section 2.1(b) imposes on the same power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of waived formalities; conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.13(e) and 9.1's final paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carefully conditioned on Lender's compliance with the Code, with four enumerated exclusions; a well-built limitation of liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.8 (insurance) and 11.3, and with the UCC reasonable-care duty preserved in the Section 9.1 chapeau.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad, with an all-caps clause extending the indemnity to an Indemnified Person's own negligence and "of any other Person," then a carve-out only for gross negligence or wilful misconduct — the interaction of those two sentences is the classic point of contest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(b) preserves an assigning Lender's rights under this Section, and Section 16.11 has its own separate indemnity with a narrower carve-out; the two indemnities are not aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deemed receipt is set at "the earlier of the date of actual receipt or three (3) Business Days after the deposit thereof in the mail," which as written makes mailing effective only if it precedes actual receipt — the ordinary formula uses "the earlier of actual receipt or three days," so the sentence works only awkwardly; the Lender's Dallas ZIP code is also given as 75244 here and 75254 in the exhibits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.4 says any writing requirement is satisfied by transmission of a Record, which is a looser standard than this Section's prescribed methods.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unqualified New York choice of law with a carve-out for contrary provisions in other Loan Documents; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.13(g) and 2.13(h) are drafted entirely around Sections 580a, 580b, 580d and 726 of the California Code of Civil Procedure, and the "Code" definition contemplates other states' UCCs governing perfection — so the instrument is not uniformly New York.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Venue is "only" in New York County for the parties, but Lender alone may sue anywhere collateral is found — a conspicuously one-sided allocation of a genuinely reciprocal-looking clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.3 forbids construing ambiguity against either party, which is the provision that would otherwise answer a contra proferentem challenge to this asymmetry.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional, mutual jury waiver with an express knowing-and-voluntary recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13(a) and 13(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All, or any ratable part of all" is odd phrasing, and the final sentence dispenses with the Eligible Transferee requirement for portfolio sales — a wide exception to the stated restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Eligible Transferee" definition gives Administrative Borrower an approval right absent an Event of Default, which the portfolio-sale exception overrides; consistent but one-directional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states that an assignment "shall effect a novation between Borrowers and the Assignee" — a strong legal consequence stated in passing and without elaboration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.2 says "No consent to assignment by Lender shall release any Borrower from its Obligations," which pulls against the novation language here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deems the Agreement amended automatically on receipt of an assignment and acceptance, without Borrower signature; short but consequential.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1 requires that every amendment "be in writing and signed by Lender and Administrative Borrower," so this automatic amendment mechanism contradicts the amendment provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and heavily itemised with five enumerated protective conditions; the final proviso is mislettered but each limb is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Participants are made Indemnified Persons under Section 11.3 while this subsection denies them any direct rights — a deliberate asymmetry rather than a conflict.
